NVIDIA selected Palantir Foundry to manage its 1.3 million-part Vera Rubin rack supply chain, making NVDA the ultimate enterprise reference customer for PLTR.

Palantir posted record Q2 revenue of $1.94 billion, up 93% year over year, yet trades at 240x earnings with a $384 billion market cap.

Jensen Huang called supply chains 'the operating system of the physical economy,' but NVIDIA's endorsement alone won't compress Palantir's lofty multiple.

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and NVIDIA made the cut. Enter your email to see the other nine names and why NVDA earned its spot. The report is free. Enter your email and see the full list.

On Wednesday morning, NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) shared a secret: it has handed the software running its 1.3 million-part supply chain inside every Vera Rubin rack to Palantir (NASDAQ:PLTR). The endorsement lands in an awkward spot for the market. Just two days earlier, on his September 8 broadcast, Jim Cramer described Palantir as "ice cold for the first half of this year" before its recent rebound. The stock is down 6.2% YTD even as NVIDIA has climbed 17.52%.

2015 Getty Images / Getty Images News via Getty Images

Palantir shares traded at $167.15 midday Thursday, down 1.41% on the session despite the news, per Barron's coverage of the expanded AI partnership.

PLTR Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.
Inside the Sovereign AI Supply Chain Deal

The expanded partnership fuses Palantir Foundry and AIP with NVIDIA Nemotron open models grounded in Palantir Ontology. NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang described the stakes, calling supply chains "the operating system of the physical economy." Palantir CEO Alex Karp said the sovereign stack is "delivering capabilities that exceed the frontier while providing alpha protection qualities unavailable otherwise."

Burry exited NVDA December puts as time decay bled premium, with NVDA up 19% YTD and CRWV's $104 billion backlog crushing the bear case.

Burry still holds 2027 puts on PLTR and QQQ, signaling his AI bear thesis remains intact even as he trims near-term hedges and sits on cash.

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and NVIDIA made the cut. Enter your email to see the other nine names and why NVDA earned its spot. The report is free. Enter your email and see the full list.

Michael Burry, the Scion Asset Management founder made famous by The Big Short, is trimming his sails. In a Substack post cited this week, Burry said he "pulled in risk" in September and now has cash he is "happy to sit on" while he watches how markets develop. The most notable change: he shed December 2026 put options on NVIDIA without rolling them into later-dated contracts, a direct reduction of his most-watched bearish AI trade.

24/7 Wall St.

That matters because Burry had built a sizable options-based short against the AI infrastructure complex, including $187 million in put options on NVIDIA as part of roughly $1 billion in bearish AI wagers disclosed earlier. Closing the December strikes tells you something about how expensive those hedges became to carry as the underlying stocks kept grinding higher. (The buildout goes well beyond the chipmakers themselves, and we profiled seven of the power, cooling, and networking suppliers benefiting from it in a free report here.)

Why Burry Is Trimming Exposure Now

Burry has not flipped bullish. He continues to hold 2027 puts on Palantir (NASDAQ:PLTR) and the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ), and told readers the exit should not be read as optimism. The stated reason for closing the December NVDA puts was rapid time-based decay. Short-dated puts bleed premium quickly when the stock refuses to break, and NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) has done anything but break.

PLTR has surged 1,693% since its 2020 IPO, yet Q2 U.S. commercial revenue exploded 149% while shares sit 4% below their year-start price.

Reaching $250 requires just 47% more upside and no multiple expansion, only EPS catching up to a FY2027 estimate of $2.31.

FY2026 EPS estimates jumped from $1.46 to $1.60 in 90 days with 25 upward analyst revisions and zero downward, signaling Wall Street is still chasing Palantir's momentum.

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and Palantir didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat PLTR. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.

Palantir (NASDAQ:PLTR) has become the defining name in enterprise AI. The stock is up 1,692.63% since its 2020 direct listing, yet shares are actually down 4.19% year to date.

Shutterstock / Piotr Swat

Meanwhile, Q2 revenue grew 92.83% year over year and U.S. commercial revenue exploded 149%. CEO Alex Karp called the quarter "otherworldly". So can PLTR keep climbing to $250 in 2027? I think the setup is more compelling than the stock price suggests.

Why Palantir Shares Are Stuck Despite Blowout Numbers

The disconnect is real. Shares are down 5.35% over the past week and 0.99% over the past month, even after a monster earnings report. The reason has less to do with the business and more to do with the stock. Palantir trades at a trailing P/E of 241x with a beta of 1.62. That is a punishing combination when rates wobble.

As MarketWatch noted last week, bond yields and competitive noise from Google have hit the multiple. Then on September 8, the stock slipped even after naming Nebius its preferred sovereign AI partner. High-beta names get sold first when investors rotate. Nothing about Q2 fundamentals justifies the pullback.
